Hair shampoos are used in conjunction with water and a toothbrush or hairbrush, as well as other agents (such as a comb or other cleaning utensil), to give hair a clean and shiny appearance. Shampoos may be used on wet or dry hair, depending on the ingredients.

History of hair shampoos
Hair shampoos originated in antiquity. Hair shampoos in ancient Egypt consisted of a water, oil and fragrant base, usually including sesame, babylon, myrrh or frankincense.
Early shampoos contained alkali, which was necessary for hair care until soap was mass-produced. The soap, with its higher alkalinity, could be used to cleanse hair without the need for the added alkali, which was needed to neutralize the acidity of the scalp oil. The earliest known example of soap for personal grooming can be found in the Sumerian clay tablets, written circa 2110 - 2050 BC, where a method for producing soap using natural lye and animal fats was described.[1] The Romans also invented soap during this time, and the use of soap for personal hygiene became widespread across Europe by the 1500s.[2]
Types of hair shampoos
Hair shampoos are made primarily from two ingredients: water and cleaning agents.
